standard_conversion: Adopt ONE internal standard: German 50%-complete-penetration ('durchschlagend') vs homogeneous RHA ~220-265 BHN at 30° from vertical — i.e. exactly what pen_ref_mm already claims to be. Conversion recipe: (1) German Jentz/Panzerbeschusstafeln figures (panzerworld tables): use as-is, factor 1.00. (2) Soviet published single-column values (GvA, battlefield.ru, most firing-table reproductions) are the PSP 'certified/guaranteed' limit (≥75-80% of shell mass behind plate): multiply by 1.12 (band 1.10-1.15). (3) Soviet PTP 'initial' limit sits ~5-6% above PSP: multiply PTP by 1.06. (4) US Army 50% criterion ≈ German 50%: factor 1.00. Caveat to encode as a comment: for large-caliber APHE the criterion gap can exceed the band (tankarchives' D-25T re-rated to the US 50% criterion reads 196/179/158/125 vs Soviet-table ~125/122/113/96 @30°) — treat 1.12 as a floor for the 122 mm and 152 mm rounds and keep their anchors flagged. Applied concretely: BR-350B 75→84, BR-354P 80→90, BR-365 97→109, BR-412B 130→146, BR-471 125→140 (floor; code's 145 acceptable), BR-540 105→118. Sources: ballistics.json model_guidance (this repo, session-verified); tankarchives.com 'Common Questions: KwK 43 vs D-25T Penetration'; Bird & Livingston 'WWII Ballistics: Armour and Gunnery' (criterion discussion); panzerworld.com/armor-penetration-table (German criterion, fetched this session).
